refuted_claims:
R1 (most important; conflicts with the owner's purpose). Claim: "Proposed layout: evolve on SearchQA, guard on OfficeQA-train (the hub of the similarity map), claim on LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld"; "the generalisation claim is made on LiveMath and SpreadsheetBench, OfficeQA's other neighbours". Checked: skillopt/coevo5/protocol.py lines 18-19 (SIMILAR_PAIRS gives SIMILAR['searchqa'] = ('officeqa',)) and the owner's 10/17 rule in memory/research-goal-generalization-no-val.md (map fixed and confirmed; readout = a pre-registered transfer matrix with pooled similar and dissimilar readouts; never redefine "similar" afterwards). Found: OfficeQA is SearchQA's ONLY registered similar bench. LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld are all dissimilar to SearchQA. The layout spends the only similar target as the guard, so the owner's central readout ("similar benches improve") is left with one guarded target and the clean claims shrink to "dissimilar benches did not drop". The same holds for every non-hub source, since LiveMath and SpreadsheetBench also have only OfficeQA as their similar bench. The hub itself cannot be the source: 74 items gives P(source pass | +5) of about 0.19, the explorer's own figure. So the real-pool guard (decision 1 = yes) cannot coexist with a clean similar-transfer claim for ANY source. Only a generated-panel guard keeps that claim clean, and v0 is invalid.

R2. Claim (verdict_cn and section 0.4): "a +5 rule ... harmless on the target: 79%; costs it 10 points: 18% (3% with 120 guard items)". Checked: e9_decision_numbers.py joint() uses guard SD 0.32 at 60/120 items; the source test is z 1.645 with a 3-point floor, no Holm step and no placebo condition. I reproduced the grid and re-simulated (E9-critic/scripts/joint_oc_check.py). Found:
(a) The RECOMMENDED guard is OfficeQA, 74 items x 2 runs, per-item SD 0.397-0.486 (the explorer's own measurement). With it, a +5/-10 rule is accepted 0.25-0.38, not 0.18. The guard removes 53-68% of such rules, not 78%/96%. 120 items is impossible on a 74-item pool.
(b) The rule AS WRITTEN (z_{1-alpha/m} with Holm over m <= 5, AND beating the best of 4 placebos; cal-1 placebo effects used) gives: a harmless +5 rule 0.53-0.58 (not 0.79); +5/-10 on the OfficeQA guard 0.17-0.28; P(source pass | +5) 0.55-0.61 (not 0.84).
The guard's relative effect is right; the absolute numbers shown to the owner belong to a configuration he is not asked to adopt.

R3. Claim: "Negative transfer between similar benchmarks is real ... Every rule needs the transfer check". Checked: plan.json arm sizes; task_cards.json (cards 1,846-2,926 chars); v3_proposals.json (rules 208-499 chars, median 386); the pilot's parent (P = empty scaffold). Found: every measured harm comes from a whole task card, 4-7x a rule's length, added to an EMPTY scaffold. The decision rule targets rules of at most 600 chars on a FIVE-SEED parent, which contains the OfficeQA card (under O_home alone, answer-only replies were 1.4%). Bleed of rule-sized text on a seeded parent is unmeasured. "Real" holds for seeds and is extrapolated for rules.

R4 (new threat, verified). Claims: "The real pool reproduces across windows (E2 10/20 vs E9 10/21)" and "the real OfficeQA training pool works as a transfer proxy". Checked: completion tokens and pass rates per session in D12's v3 training-side table (/data/feasibility/D12/v3_train_side_cells.json), the E2 records and the E9 cells; per-item prompt_tokens in v3 versus E9. Found: OfficeQA answering switches between session-level regimes.
- Both replicating windows were in a "computing" regime: empty-scaffold median completion 167 / 184.5 tokens, short-reply share 0.23 / 0.22.
- In the v3 run, 8 of 9 OfficeQA units were "answer-only" (median 10-11 tokens, 64-88% of replies at 20 tokens or fewer) for EVERY arm in the unit. The five-seed I-ds parent on the same 60 items: s3 screen 232 tokens, pass 0.508; s4 screen/confirm 10 tokens, pass 0.267.
- Same Skill hash (cc516459), same 74 items, identical prompt_tokens on 74 of 74: E9 window minus v3 window = +20.3 points (SE 5.2; 19 up / 3 down).
The harm E9 found (texts push OfficeQA to answer-only replies) is the very variable that flips by session. In an answer-only session the parent already answers only, so the harm cannot show. Veto decisions are therefore regime-conditional. Interleaving removes level shifts but not this text-by-session interaction. Cross-window replication was shown only within one regime: 2 windows, 3 texts.

R5. Claim: the guard follows "reusable-holdout / Ladder logic (Dwork et al. 2015, Thresholdout; Blum & Hardt 2015)". Checked: arXiv 1506.02629 and PMLR v37. Found: the citations are correct, but Thresholdout's guarantee rests on Laplace noise added to the threshold and to the answers, and the description-length bound degrades by a factor 2^k. A deterministic, noise-free veto on a reused 74-item pool inherits neither. A Hoeffding plus 2^k bound at a 10-point tolerance needs roughly 300-500 items for 5-10 released bits. This is an analogy, not a guarantee. verdict_cn's "不会变成训练信号" (it never becomes a training signal) overstates; the report itself says up to 5T veto bits shape the next parent.

R6 (cost). Claims: per-cell "SearchQA 1,300 / 3,850", OfficeQA seeded "8,200-8,856", "per step 1.1-3.6M". Checked: the 'charged' column of the cal-1 TSV, and the E2 records. Found:
- 1,300 / 3,850 are cal-1 MEDIANS (1,264 / 3,846). The means are 2,780 (scaffold) and 4,669 (ids-full), 2.1x and 1.2x higher.
- 8,200-8,856 is the one-card O_home arm. A five-seed parent adds about 9 KB of Skill, roughly 2,300 prompt tokens per cell. An OfficeQA guard arm is then about 1.6M (not 1.21M), and a step with 1-2 passers about 3.3-5.0M (not 2.4-3.6M).
- The acceptance rule as written also needs 4 placebo arms on the 300x2 source panel, about 11M per step. The full E9 rule is about 20-30M per step; the guard is about 10-20% of it.

R7 (minor). verdict_cn calls the two L_home vetoes "two different time periods, consistent": they used the same 74 items in the same regime, both bounds were marginal (UB -0.51 / -0.98), and the explorer concedes "partly luck". The answer-only share is 0.597 / 0.592 in the report versus 0.581 / 0.568 from the cells' own flag (definitional; immaterial).

E2: S_home +6.0 (SE 2.87) on LiveMath and -4.05 on OfficeQA; S_general +10.81; L_home -8.11; O_home +13.51. The E2 window's P (0.392) matches E9's (0.405).

D12 session means: 0.508 / 0.267 / 0.267 / 0.342.

Bibliography is correct: Dwork et al., Science 349(6248), 2015; Blum & Hardt, ICML 2015, PMLR 37.

The explorer's honest caveats also hold:
- the per-rule guard is only a gross-harm screen;
- the result is moot on v3 (0 accepted);
- whole-pool reuse on OfficeQA (74), SpreadsheetBench (120) and ALFWorld (57) amounts to a fixed validation set;
- veto-only is right, and "must help the target" or per-rule non-inferiority are rightly rejected.

Not re-checked: C4' operating characteristics (D8/D12), the SHA identity of S_home with cal-1 seed-only, and the pool sizes 600 / 283 / 120 / 57.
missing:
1. Structural consequence of the map: OfficeQA is the only similar bench of every non-hub source. Any real-pool guard therefore costs the clean similar-transfer readout, and the generated panel is the ONLY claim-clean route. That route is exactly the verification-side (co-evolution) bottleneck, so the next work should go there, not into a real-pool guard.

2. OfficeQA session regime (+20.3 points for the same text across windows): diagnose the cause (route or backend, time) before any OfficeQA-based gate or readout. Otherwise pin the regime, or require a guard decision to hold in 2 windows, which doubles the cost and lowers power. The regime also affects the final OfficeQA test readouts and the good-instruction baseline: on the v3 OfficeQA training unit the five-seed I-ds parent was only +4.7 (SE 3.2) over the empty scaffold, against +13.5 / +17.6 for the OfficeQA card alone in computing windows. Whether that gap is bleed or regime is unresolved.

3. Co-evolution (purpose 1) is only a measurement here, not a mechanism. Validity criterion (b), attenuation against the real pool, itself uses the target's training items. If the generator evolves and is re-validated against OfficeQA-train every step, that pool becomes the verification side's validation set, and the same owner rule applies.

4. Generated-panel design:
- Criterion (a) must be measured under the SEEDED parent (O_home already passes 0.964 on G).
- "Keep items the parent fails at least once" is the wrong filter for a harm detector: it removes the reliably passed items where a break shows.
- The missed L_home harm arises because G items need no multi-step computation, so difficulty should be set by construction (at least 2 operations, D6 typed specs).

5. Base rate unknown: how often does a rule-sized text cost 10 or more points on a similar target? If rarely, the per-rule guard's expected value is small. The explorer's pilot #5 should use the REAL pool, rule-sized texts, a five-seed parent, and 2 windows (to test regime dependence).

6. Literature not used:
- Gulrajani & Lopez-Paz, ICLR 2021 (DomainBed): selecting with target-domain data is oracle test-domain validation and must be declared. This supports the "guarded" label and also bars a domain-generalisation claim on that target.
- Thomas et al., ICML 2015 (HCPI), and Thomas et al., Science 2019 (Seldonian): the safety test puts the burden on proving no harm. E9 reverses it, so it gives no assurance below about 10 points; say so plainly.
- Sclar et al., ICLR 2024 (formatting sensitivity up to 76 points) and Chen, Zaharia & Zou 2023 (same-prompt behaviour drift over time): precedents for the cal-1 placebo shifts and for the regime drift.

7. Full-rule cost: placebo arms, mean (not median) per-cell cost and the five-seed prompt overhead. See R6: about 20-30M per step for the whole acceptance rule.
notes_cn:
结论：部分成立。数字基本都对，但推荐的做法和您的目标有冲突。可行性应从"中等"降为"低"。

我核对过、确认没错的：
- E9 的试验一共 1124 次解题，没有失败的，有 12 次因回答太长被截断。我从原始记录重算了一遍，每个数都对得上。
- 校准实验（11 段技能文本 × 200 道 SearchQA 训练题 × 4 次，共 8800 次）的数字也全部一致。
- "LiveMath 的任务说明会让 OfficeQA 掉约 9 分"属实。
- "自动出的仿 OfficeQA 题太简单"也属实：空白技能就能做对 89%。

主要问题（按重要程度排）：

1. 推荐方案用掉了唯一的"相似基准"。
- 按您 10/17 确认的相似关系，和 SearchQA 相似的只有 OfficeQA 一个。
- E9 建议"在 SearchQA 上进化，用 OfficeQA 的训练题做检查"。这样 OfficeQA 就被"用过"了，不能再干净地证明"相似基准也涨分"。
- 它说"结论在 LiveMath、SpreadsheetBench 上下"。但这两个对 SearchQA 来说都是"不相似"的，只能证明"不相似的没掉分"。
- 其实从任何一个基准进化，相似的都只有 OfficeQA。OfficeQA 自己只有 74 道训练题，又不能拿来进化。
- 所以"用真实训练题做检查"和"证明相似基准涨分"不能同时做到。唯一干净的办法是"自动出题"，而它现在还不合格。

2. 给您的接受概率偏乐观。
- 报告里"无害规则约 79% 被接受，掉 10 分的只有 18%（用 120 道题检查时 3%）"，是按题目更稳定的 60 或 120 道题算的。
- 推荐的 OfficeQA 只有 74 道题，120 道根本凑不出来。按推荐方案重算：掉 10 分的规则仍有 25% 到 38% 会被接受。
- 再按它自己写的完整规则算（同时测 5 条要更严，还要比 4 段无关文字的对照组分数高），无害的好规则只有 53% 到 58% 能通过。

3. 我新发现的问题：OfficeQA 上模型的答题习惯会随时段整段切换。
- 同一段技能文本、同样 74 道题、模型收到的输入一模一样。
- 在 v3（第三版实验）那几天，模型几乎都只回一个短答案。回答长度的中位数约 10 个 token（token 是模型读写文字的计量单位）。
- 在 E2、E9 试验的那两晚，模型会列算式计算，中位数约 170 到 185 个 token。
- 两个时段正确率差了 20.3 分。v3 里 9 段 OfficeQA 测量，有 8 段是"只给答案"模式。
- E9 发现的伤害，恰恰就是"让模型改成只给答案"。在"只给答案"的时段里，这种伤害根本测不出来。
- 所以一次检查的结论，换个时段可能就不成立。E9 说的"两次测量结果一致"，两次都恰好落在"列算式"的时段。

4. 证据和要检查的东西不一样。
- 掉分是用整段任务说明（约 1800 到 2900 个字符）、加在空白技能上测出来的。
- 真正要检查的是不超过 600 字符的规则，而且技能里已经有五段任务说明。这种情况下会不会掉分，还没测过。

5. 成本算少了。
- 它用的单次解题花费是中位数，平均花费要高 1.2 到 2.1 倍。
- 它自己写的规则还要在源基准上多跑 4 段对照文字，每一步约 1100 万 token。
- 整套规则每一步约 2000 万到 3000 万 token，检查本身只占一到两成。

6. 引用的两篇论文书目都对，但保证不适用。
- 这两篇（Dwork 2015、Blum 与 Hardt 2015）讲的是"同一批留出题能否反复使用"。它们的保证要靠加随机噪声和足够多的题目。74 道题、不加噪声的情况下不适用，只能算类比。
- 有两类相关文献它没用：
  - 域泛化研究：拿目标基准的数据来挑方法，算"偷看答案"，必须声明（Gulrajani 与 Lopez-Paz 2021）。
  - 安全改进方法：要先证明无害才接受（Thomas 2015、2019）。E9 正好反过来，要证明有害才否决，所以对 10 分以下的伤害基本没有保护。

值得保留的部分：
- 对每条规则做一次便宜的"格式大破坏"筛查，用自动出的新题，每一步约 30 万 token。这不需要验证集，能拦住"答案格式丢失"这类大问题。试验里一段放错位置的说明掉了 33 分，就被它拦下了。
- 先查清 OfficeQA 时段切换的原因，比如接口背后是不是换了机器或模型版本。查清之前，OfficeQA 上的任何对比都不稳。

需要您决定的一件事：是否接受"相似基准涨分"只能靠自动出题来检查？如果接受，下一步的重点就是把自动出题做难、做准。这正是您说的"验证端进化"的那一半。
